speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: How long have you had this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg, and what does the wound look like? Do you see any drainage, odor, or signs of spreading redness?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history. Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent steroid use, along with the initial ant bite, are you experiencing fever, chills, or any systemic symptoms of infection? Also, does the pain radiate or is it localized strictly to the wound?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, ESR, and Blood Glucose.
REQUEST IMAGES: Color photos of the ulcer and surrounding tissue.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Normal; Blood_Glucose_Level Random Elevated; CRP: Not Available; ESR: Not Available

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the necrotic base, purplish irregular borders, history of an ant bite, pitting edema, and your significant risk factors for vasculopathy and immunosuppression, I suspect this is a necrotic ulcer caused by cutaneous anthrax or a severe necrotizing infection secondary to vasculitis. Given the urgency you expressed, I will not ask further questions; please proceed to the Emergency Department immediately for surgical debridement and IV antibiotics while we await your image results.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Necrotizing Cutaneous Anthrax (secondary to ant bite) or Severe Necrotizing Cellulitis/Pyoderma Gangrenosum
